headline: High: social-auto-upload can exfiltrate dbt-produced warehouse data via broad egress, while shared-file and injection risks are otherwise limited by missing write/read surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented: dbt-core has no shared channel or output parser surface, and social-auto-upload shows only CLI/headless automation with file inputs. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or file handoff, so the pathway exists but is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies dbt-generated text into social-auto-upload inputs or captions
IF both agents are connected through a shared manual clipboard or file handoff
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste dbt output into upload captions or prompts
Use a review step before any text from dbt reaches social-auto-upload
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for transferred text

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, while social-auto-upload has broad egress and handles account data plus media files. Even without a shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive warehouse-derived content into an external upload path in default workflows, creating a realistic leakage route.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs warehouse-derived data into files or text later consumed by social-auto-upload
IF social-auto-upload uploads content containing sensitive warehouse data to external platforms
mitigations: Restrict dbt outputs to non-sensitive datasets
Review upload payloads before posting
Use separate service accounts for warehouse and social platforms
Mask or redact sensitive fields before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call data-warehouse APIs, while social-auto-upload can call biliup and has broad egress, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git state, or shared mutable resource. The main conflict is indirect and limited to separate external APIs, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through separate APIs
IF an operator maps dbt outputs into the same account or upload queue used by social-auto-upload
mitigations: Assign distinct accounts and API credentials
Avoid shared output directories
Run the agents in separate sessions
Document ownership of each mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can generate warehouse-derived outputs that social-auto-upload may treat as upload content, and the latter has no documented verification step for upstream facts. That makes a mistaken dbt artifact plausibly cascade into an external post or upload, though the pair does not show autonomous downstream action beyond the upload workflow.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes dbt-generated text, metadata, or files as authoritative upload inputs
IF no human review occurs before the upload action
mitigations: Require human approval before posting
Validate dbt outputs against source data
Use a checksum or schema check on transferred artifacts
Separate generation from publishing steps
requires-engineering: add explicit verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core processes data warehouse data, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads media to third-party social platforms. The pair creates a plausible residency/retention mismatch if warehouse data or regulated content is transferred into social uploads; no profile shows a built-in compliance boundary, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is transferred into social-auto-upload inputs
IF the target social platform or hosting path has different retention or residency rules than the warehouse
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of upload content
Review platform retention settings
Use region-appropriate storage for intermediate files
Maintain a data-class mapping for each upload
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
